The Treaty of Tordesillas was a diplomatic agreement between Spain and Portugal to resolve territorial disputes arising from their voyages of exploration and claims over newly discovered lands outside Europe. It specifically drew a line of demarcation in the Atlantic Ocean to divide the world into Spanish and Portuguese spheres of influence. This was a direct outcome of European maritime exploration in the late 15th century, particularly following Columbus’s 1492 voyage.  

The African slave trade (B) was underway but not the central issue here; the treaty focused on territorial claims. The Scientific Revolution (C) and the Protestant Reformation (D) came later and were not directly related to this 1494 treaty.  

Final answer: (A)
